description: This chart displays three pie charts labeled “easy,” “medium,” and “hard,” each representing the distribution of four categories—N+K+, N−K+, N−K−, and N+K−—under a “Zero-Shot” evaluation. Each pie chart contains four distinct colored segments: teal for N+K+, tan for N−K+, brown for N−K−, and reddish-brown for N+K−. The “easy” chart shows the largest segment (teal, N+K+) at 55.4%, followed by tan (N−K+) at 38.3%, then reddish-brown (N+K−) at 4.6%, and the smallest segment (brown, N−K−) at 1.7%. The “medium” chart shows the largest segment (teal, N+K+) at 58.8%, followed by tan (N−K+) at 35.4%, then reddish-brown (N+K−) at 4.8%, and the smallest segment (brown, N−K−) at 1.8%. The “hard” chart shows the largest segment (tan, N−K+) at 37.9%, followed by teal (N+K+) at 37.3%, then reddish-brown (N+K−) at 6.7%, and the smallest segment (brown, N−K−) at 18.1%. A legend on the right confirms the color-to-category mapping. Each slice includes its percentage value printed inside, and the segments are arranged in descending order of size within each pie chart.
